title.en: present and past participle clauses · Having + past participle

explain.ko: 분사 구문은 접속사와 주어를 줄여서 두 절을 간결하게 연결하는 구조입니다. 두 절의 주어가 같을 때 쓸 수 있습니다. 현재분사(-ing)는 동시 동작이나 이유를 나타냅니다(Waiting for the bus, she read a book). Having + 과거분사는 앞선 행동을 나타냅니다(Having finished his work, he went home). 과거분사는 수동의 의미를 나타냅니다(Written in 1990, the book is still popular). 부정은 Not + 분사입니다(Not knowing the reason, he left). 주어가 다르면 분사의 주어를 따로 써야 하며 이것을 독립분사구문이라고 합니다.
explain.en: Participle clauses join two clauses concisely by dropping the conjunction and subject, when both clauses have the same subject. The -ing form shows simultaneous action or reason (Waiting for the bus, she read a book). Having + past participle shows an earlier action (Having finished his work, he went home). The past participle has a passive meaning (Written in 1990, the book is still popular). Negative: Not + participle (Not knowing the reason, he left). If the subjects differ, the participle needs its own subject (an absolute clause).

notes.ko: 분사의 주어와 주절의 주어는 반드시 같아야 합니다. 다르면 틀린 문장이 됩니다.
notes.en: The participle's subject must match the main clause subject, or the sentence is wrong.

notes.ko: 접속사(while, after, because)를 남겨 의미를 분명히 할 수 있습니다. While waiting …
notes.en: You can keep a conjunction for clarity: While waiting …

notes.ko: 격식 있는 글에서 자주 쓰이며 말할 때는 잘 쓰지 않습니다.
notes.en: Common in formal writing, rare in speech.
